title: Droplet Open Ring
category: Ring (adjustable open ring with 2 different ends, 1 round ball and 1 teardrop, no stones, no setting; sold as 1 piece)
metal: Two variants: 18k gold tone (PVD 18K gold coating) or rhodium silver tone (PVD rhodium coating), both over surgical stainless steel, anti-tarnish (listing). Finish: mirror polish all over, no texture, no stones, no engraving. Photos by metal: 01 and 02 are 18k gold tone, 03, 04 and 05 are rhodium silver tone, 07 (size guide) is the gold supplier photo. This card shoots rhodium silver tone.
lock: 1 adjustable open ring of slim round polished wire, no stones. 2 different ends sit side by side on top of the finger, almost touching: 1 round ball on a short flared neck, and 1 long smooth teardrop, 6.6 mm wide, its fat rounded end beside the ball. Rhodium silver tone, mirror polish. Must stay 1 ball beside 1 teardrop, never 2 matching ends or a closed band.
morph: The teardrop end. Image models like symmetry, so they redraw it as a second ball (from the front the teardrop's fat end really does read as a ball: listing photo 05 nearly looks like 2 balls), or swing it round to face the ball point-first, curl its tip into a hook (the E2 silver hero did this), or blow it up to twice the ball. Second risk: the 2 ends pulled apart across a wide gap (they almost touch), or the gap closed into a plain band. Third: scale. The colour-50 ad 44 ('Raindrop, made silver.', 9.3) was flagged 'reads large' in REDO43. Also watch for an invented bezel, stone or pearl on the ball.
sizeMm: Listed (description and size guide 07): teardrop about 6.6 mm at its widest; weight about 4.6 g; open, adjusts to fit US 5 to 9 (by the standard US chart that is about 15.7 to 18.9 mm inside); size guide says 'give or take 1 mm'. The ball size is not listed, so never print a ball mm. Estimated (not listed): from 01 and 02 the ball is about as wide as the teardrop's fat end; the teardrop is about twice as long as it is wide (about 12 mm with its taper); the wire is about 2 mm (photos plus the 4.6 g weight); the gap between ball and drop is under 1 mm. Body referent: both ends together sit across the top of 1 finger, about as wide as the finger; each end is about the size of a green pea, a little over half a fingernail wide. Worn photo 04 reads close to true (perhaps slightly generous); 05 reads true.

story: A ball and a drop, almost touching (the listing's own first line). It is one bead of liquid metal caught at 2 moments: the drop that has landed and gone round, and the drop still falling, a breath apart. That near-touch is the whole drama: a full stop beside a comma, the 2 fingers in Michelangelo's Creation of Adam, 2 raindrops on a window about to merge. Rhymes, from safest to craziest: water beading on a lotus leaf (colour-50 ad 44 'Raindrop, made silver.' scored 9.3, kept off only for reading large); a glass serum dropper with 1 silver bead hanging off its tip ('the only drop in your routine that never runs out'); a mercury bead, chrome, liquid metal; ink falling off a fountain-pen nib next to the full stop it already made; a tap mid-drip; a Newton's cradle ball; a drop of attar off a glass dauber or of rose water from a gulabpash; a single moti and a ghee drop off a spoon; the Hindi 'boond' (drop) and 'boond boond se sagar banta hai' (drop by drop, an ocean); boondi, the sweet whose name means little drops; a semicolon turned on its side; the musical eighth note (a ball on a stem). Sibling: it pairs with the Droplet Open Cuff in the same metal (the listing says so), so ring and cuff make a set or a BUY2. Fit is a selling point: 1 ring opens to fit US 5 to 9, so no sizing guesswork and an easy gift (earlier ads-500 board ideas: 'One ring, five sizes', 'Measured, not rounded', 'Flip your wrist'). Waterproof and tarnish free: a never-take-it-off ring. Listing styling: bare hands, ivory linen, hand raised to the face.
